title: One execution service: single run/status/rerun over the existing engine
description:
Slice B of avg-qr4.2, the heart of it.

studio/runtime/src/engine/ contains StageExecutor and StageStateMachine with leases, attempts and validated transitions. Verified: zero production call sites outside their own module. The same is true of checkGate/checkGates, BudgetLedger, propagateStaleness and ArtifactStore. A tested engine exists and nothing calls it.

Three active paths each reimplement a shallower, mutually incompatible 'run':
- studio/runtime/src/cli.ts cmdRun persists nothing — it picks the first stage with a missing output file and prints an instruction string for the agent.
- studio/gateway/src/runtime/executor.ts runAutopilot actually executes handlers and writes artifacts.
- studio/agent/src/pipeline-tools.ts describes tools as executing and waiting.

Scope: one ExecutionService with a single meaning for run/status/rerun, built on the existing engine plus slice A's store. Fail closed on unknown stages, empty outputs, expired leases, missing budget reservations and dependency failures. Dry-run performs no writes and no paid calls.
notes:
PR #4: https://github.com/phoebus-84/video-studio/pull/4 (branch qr4.2b-execution-service, 17 commits).

Serial tests: contracts 116, runtime 410 across 36 files, gateway 278, agent 184 — all green; typechecks and runtime build clean.

Ships with no production caller by design; avg-2n7 and avg-grf are what make the acceptance criterion literally true. Second slice in a row to land unused.

No approval gate, deliberately: that belongs to avg-qr4.3, and wiring a third interpretation before it decides what an approval is would be the mistake this issue exists to fix.

Four bugs fixed that were defects in this branch's own spec or plan, each reproduced before fixing: a failed stage never released its lease (pre-existing, untested); one dispatcher failure deadlocked the whole episode; the retry cap counted successes and stranded a stage with a false message; and a late write after a lease takeover made the episode permanently underivable on an append-only journal.

Follow-ups: avg-91o (budget reservations leak), avg-h2q (wall-clock lease tests), avg-d43 (StageExecutor is dead code).
close_reason:
Merged to main as PR #4 (merge commit 861141f). Merged tree verified: contracts 116, runtime 410 across 36 files, gateway 278, agent 184 — all green.

Delivered: ExecutionService with one meaning for run/status/rerun; state from journal replay with no file-existence inference; dispatch and budget as injected ports so absence is refusal; the fail-closed matrix; dry run that sees every gate and returns would-run; rerun that pre-validates its ids.

Fixed along the way, each reproduced first: a failed stage never released its lease (pre-existing); one dispatcher failure deadlocked the whole episode; the retry cap counted successes; and a late write after a lease takeover made an episode permanently underivable.

On the record: ships with no production caller. avg-2n7 and avg-grf are what make qr4.2's acceptance criterion literally true.

title: Durable execution state: persist stage instances, attempts, and leases
description:
Slice A of avg-qr4.2.

StageInstance lives only in an in-memory Map inside StageExecutor. Nothing persists it. rerun/recovery.ts and rerun/planner.ts both TAKE Map<string, StageInstance> as an argument — they consume state that nothing in the project produces. The attempts/ directory is named in the layout contract (studio/contracts/src/layout.mjs) and created by workspace init, but nothing has ever written to it; real episodes under library/ have no attempts/ directory at all.

Consequence: avg-qr4.2's 'restart recovery is deterministic' is not a wiring job. There is no state to recover.

Scope: a durable store for stage instances, attempts and leases under the episode's attempts/, with a schema in @studio/contracts, atomic writes, and a load path that reconstructs the executor's Map. Lease expiry must be derivable after a restart. Everything else in qr4.2 depends on this.
notes:
PR #3: https://github.com/phoebus-84/video-studio/pull/3 (branch qr4.2a-durable-execution-state, 16 commits). Closes avg-i1x too.

Serial test results: contracts 116, runtime 360/31 files, gateway 278, agent 184 — all green; typechecks clean. See avg-82z for why the aggregate root run is not a trustworthy gate.

Ships a library with no production caller by design — avg-tt7 (slice B) is its consumer and cannot be built until this state exists.

Two defects were found only by the whole-branch review, both in the spec rather than in any implementation: the gateway wrote execution events with no leaseId that made an episode's state underivable forever, and the replay's transition table was byte-identical to the engine's when it needed to diverge (the engine governs one in-memory run; the journal is cumulative across runs, and re-running a completed stage is a first-class operation).
close_reason:
Merged to main as PR #3 (merge commit a3b5f83). Merged tree verified: contracts 116, runtime 360, gateway 278, all green.

Delivered: the journal writer conforms to its schema with real-output ajv conformance testing; execution-event payload schema with required leaseId/attemptNumber; deriveExecutionState replaying the journal deterministically and failing closed on undeclared stages, unopened attempts and forbidden transitions; lease expiry applied during replay so a crashed holder's stage becomes retryable rather than locked; and a filesystem Lock implementing the port that had only ever had a test fixture.

On the record: this slice has no production caller. avg-tt7 is its consumer.

title: Journal writer does not conform to journal-event.schema.json
description:
studio/contracts/src/journal.mjs names schemas/v1alpha1/journal-event.schema.json as its contract but has never produced conforming events. A real event from buildJournalEvent fails validation on nine counts: missing apiVersion, kind, id, episodeRef and data; eventId instead of id (a UUID where the schema requires ^evt_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$); episode instead of episodeRef; detail instead of data; stageId at top level instead of inside data; and additionalProperties is false, so the surplus keys are rejected as well.

Invisible because nothing validates journal events at runtime. scripts/check-event-fixtures.mjs validates only the four hand-written fixtures under fixtures/event/valid/, which were authored to match the schema — so the fixtures pass while every event the gateway executor actually appends would fail.

The apiVersion/kind envelope is used by 8 of the 12 schemas in studio/contracts, so the schema reflects the project convention and the writer is the shortcut. Reconcile by fixing the writer, not the schema; changing the envelope convention deserves an ADR rather than a quiet edit.

Blast radius: journal.mjs and its .d.mts, studio/contracts/test/journal.test.mjs, studio/gateway/src/runtime/executor.ts, the gateway route that serves the journal, the Pi tool that reads it, and studio/gateway/test/captions-journal.test.ts.

Add runtime validation as part of the fix so the two cannot silently diverge again.

Found while implementing avg-qr4.1, which builds gate-review records on the writer's current shape rather than blocking on this.
notes: Scope addition from avg-pm8's design (2026-09-16): also delete the redundant attempt-recorded write at studio/gateway/src/runtime/executor.ts:601. Its payload is { durationMs, outputs } with no leaseId or attemptNumber, because the gateway takes no leases. Once this issue adds runtime validation and avg-pm8 makes attempt-recorded lease-bound, that write becomes invalid and an episode halted at a review gate would fail to record. It is already redundant — the approval-requested emitted beside it by requestReview carries the same outputs with hashes, and is what the review path reads. Only durationMs is lost, and nothing consumes it.
close_reason: Done as tasks 1-2 of the avg-pm8 branch (commits e23bba0, 2b6a59a, fae0c7c). The writer now emits the schema's envelope — apiVersion, kind, evt_ ULID id, episodeRef, data, stageId inside the payload — and a contracts test runs REAL writer output through ajv, which is the check whose absence let the two drift. parseJournal gained a strict mode for callers deriving state from the log. The gateway's redundant attempt-recorded write was deleted. A later fix wave added required-field checks for the five execution payloads, closing the same drift one layer down.

title: Implement authenticated revision-bound human approval
description: P0 from docs/harness-review.md: cmdApprove records actor human regardless of caller and approvals are not bound to plan/attempt/artifact revisions. Add authenticated approval receipts that distinguish human approval, agent assessment, and policy auto-acceptance. Bind each receipt to the immutable snapshot, candidate/source hash, settings, and gate; invalidate it on relevant changes. Agent and headless calls may request approval but may not mint a human receipt.
acceptance_criteria: An agent-only call cannot satisfy a human gate. A stale receipt cannot authorize a new render or paid action. Print/headless mode stops with an explicit approval request. Browser/TUI identity, actor, timestamp, decision, justification, and bound hashes are journaled and tested.
notes:
Two things avg-2n7 makes load-bearing for this issue:

1. NOTHING WRITES approval-requested any more. The old gateway loop wrote it when blocking (executor.ts:543 in the deleted code), so an operator could see 'this is awaiting you' in the journal. The execution service never wrote those records and runAutopilot is gone. Safety is covered — a dependency with no record now falls through to the manifest rule and refuses — but the human-visible request is gone. Whoever defines what an approval IS should define how one is asked for.

2. THE SERVICE HAS NO WAY TO EXPRESS 'A HUMAN IS ATTENDING'. gates.autopilot: false is now enforced (it was not, before avg-2n7 — verified 'autopilot' appeared nowhere in service.ts). So script, compose and safety-review cannot run via ANY caller, including a human explicitly running vpr run --stage script. This is parity with what qr4.1 shipped, not a regression — its loop blocked them unconditionally too — but it means those stages are unrunnable until this issue lands an authenticated approval, or someone adds an attended-run option.
avg-grf raises BOTH walls this issue has to take down, and the CLI now runs into them.

1. ATTENDANCE. The autopilot gate refuses claim(), not just run(). So `vpr run --stage script`
   is refused -- a HUMAN being told they may not take the very stage `autopilot: false` exists
   to reserve for a human. Five stages declare `review: human`. Whatever this issue decides an
   approval is, it also has to decide how an attended actor announces itself, because claim()
   is where that now matters.

2. APPROVAL. Nothing in the current composition writes an `approval-requested` record. The
   gate-enforcement test that asserted such a record names by hash what it wants reviewed has
   no object to make and is marked inline (not silently dropped). ExecutionService.status()
   also reports review state asymmetrically -- left alone in avg-grf on purpose.

Also unreconciled vocabularies: the web contract spells the stage status `awaiting_approval`
while the service emits `awaiting_review`.

title: Monorepo shipped at ../video-studio; migrate remaining plan
description:
The eleven repositories were consolidated into /Users/euripide/strange_things/video-studio on 2026-08-14, with all 335 commits preserved via git subtree. ADR-0032 records the decision and supersedes ADR-0022.

Layout: packages/* (reusable outside the project — voice, fal-media, graphics, infographics, video-composer) and studio/* (contracts, runtime, pipelines, agent, gateway, web). Enforced by tools/check-boundaries.mjs: packages/ may not depend on studio/, and no workspace may reach into another by relative path.

Composition happens at install time: compose.config.json declares components, capabilities and requirements; five profiles (full, studio, headless, voice, render); tools/compose.mjs writes composed.json. It never substitutes a provider and refuses when two components claim one capability.

Install is: bun install && npm run compose && npm run doctor.

Three ADR-0026 violations were fixed as part of the move — the pipelines linter, the gateway's three-path CLI guess plus PATH fallback, and the gateway executor's relative import of the composer with a Homebrew Cellar glob for ffprobe.

Test state in the monorepo: 6 of 10 modules fully green. Remaining, all pre-existing:
- packages/fal-media 25/134 — index.ts exports FalClientImpl which does not exist (client.ts exports FalClient with a different constructor). The tests describe a DI client (config, contracts, clock, sleeper, logger) that was never implemented. This is fma-50i and is real design work, not a rename.
- studio/gateway 2/156 — GET /health, GET /ws token rejection.
- packages/video-composer 1/146 — normalizeMedia returns original when no change needed.
- studio/agent 1/106 — needs ImageMagick installed.
Builds still failing: @av/fal-media (4 TS errors incl. the above), @studio/gateway (18 TS errors, mostly overloads in routes/editor.ts).

title: CI: run typecheck and tests for every module on push
description:
CI exists in 1 of 11 modules (qwen-tts-worker has 4 workflows; everything else has none). The install breakage, the 25 failing fal tests, and the stale schema all survived because nothing runs.

Steps:
1. Add .github/workflows/ci.yml at the repo root: bun install once at the workspace root, then matrix over the 11 module dirs running their check/typecheck/test scripts.
2. Make the job fail on any module failure (no continue-on-error).
3. Add a job asserting no symlink or tracked file contains an absolute path outside the repo (guards regression of the E0 install bug).

Acceptance: a PR that reintroduces a file: link with an absolute target, or breaks any module's tests, goes red.

Added .github/workflows/ci.yml: a 'paths' job running check:paths, plus a fail-fast:false matrix over all 10 TS modules running typecheck and test after one root bun install. ffmpeg/imagemagick installed for the two modules that shell out to them. title: Root bun workspace: one install, relative links, no foreign absolute paths
description:
THE blocking bug. The runtime's only real cross-module link is dangling.

Reproduce:
  cd video-pipeline-runtime && npm test
  -> 20/28 test files fail: Cannot find package '@video-studio/workspace-contracts/src/vocabulary.mjs'
  readlink node_modules/@video-studio/workspace-contracts/package.json
  -> /Users/alcibiade/strange_things/avg/video-workspace-contracts/package.json

Steps:
1. Add a root package.json with a bun workspace covering all 11 module dirs (ADR-0031 mandates bun).
2. Give video-workspace-contracts an exports map so subpath imports are declared, not incidental:
   "exports": { ".": "./src/vocabulary.mjs", "./src/*": "./src/*", "./schemas/*": "./schemas/*", "./fixtures/*": "./fixtures/*" }
   (src/vocabulary.mjs is the path the runtime actually imports today.)
3. Replace the file:../ dependency links with workspace: protocol so the package manager resolves siblings internally instead of writing absolute symlinks.
4. rm -rf every module node_modules and reinstall once from the root.
5. Delete the 6 stray package-lock.json files (fal, graphics, remotion, composer, and the duplicates in pi-video-agent and gateway). Lockfile audit 2026-08-14: bun.lock only = contracts, runtime, built-in-pipelines, web; package-lock.json only = fal, graphics, remotion, composer; BOTH = pi-video-agent, gateway.

Acceptance:
- find . -type l -not -path '*/.git/*' | xargs -I{} readlink {} | grep -c '^/Users' == 0
- cd video-pipeline-runtime && npm test -> 0 import failures
- exactly one lockfile kind in the repo
close_reason:
Done. Root bun workspace added (package.json with 10 TS modules); contracts given an exports map + files list; runtime dep switched from file:../ to workspace:*; all module node_modules, 6 package-lock.json and 6 module bun.lock removed; single root install.

Result: the dangling /Users/alcibiade symlinks are gone and the import that broke the runtime resolves.
  video-pipeline-runtime BEFORE: 20/28 test files failed at import, 103 tests discovered, 5 failing.
  video-pipeline-runtime AFTER:  28/28 files pass, 339/339 tests pass.
236 tests were never being collected.

Also added scripts/check-no-foreign-paths.mjs (npm run check:paths) which fails on any symlink escaping the repo or any tracked file hardcoding a home path, scanning the root repo AND each module repo (needed because ADR-0022 gives each module its own git repo, so root git ls-files cannot see them).

title: E0 Toolchain: the workspace must install, build, and be proven by CI
description:
Prerequisite phase discovered by the 2026-08-14 architecture review. E1's own exit criteria ('bun run check green in contracts and runtime') CANNOT currently pass, because the workspace does not install on any machine but the one it was authored on.

Evidence (measured 2026-08-14):
- video-pipeline-runtime/node_modules/@video-studio/workspace-contracts/* are absolute symlinks into /Users/alcibiade/... (a different user's home). Every file in the linked package is a dangling link.
- Consequence: 20 of 28 runtime test FILES fail at import with: Cannot find package '@video-studio/workspace-contracts/src/vocabulary.mjs'. Only 5 of 103 tests are genuine assertion failures; the rest never ran.
- video-workspace-contracts/package.json declares no main, no exports, no files.
- There is no root package.json, no workspace, no Makefile, no install script.
- CI exists in 1 of 11 modules (qwen-tts-worker only). Nothing would have caught any of the above.

This epic must land before E1, or E1 cannot be verified.

Exit criteria: a fresh clone on a different machine runs one documented command and reaches green typecheck+test in every module; no absolute path outside the repo appears in any lockfile, symlink, or tracked file.
close_reason: E0 complete. The workspace now installs from one root command and CI proves it. avg-ors.1/.2/.3 all closed; see avg-uop for the now-visible true test baseline.

title: Series and channel canon must reach the prompt
description:
The channel and series knowledge directories exist, are scaffolded on creation, and are read by nothing. Canon has a shelf and no reader.

## Verified 2026-09-23

`studio/agent/src/workspace-authoring.ts` creates `visual-bible.md` with a single line of content (`# Visual Bible for <title>`) plus `characters/`, `brand/`, `references/`, `voices/`, `templates/`, `sources/`. `layout.mjs` declares them as `CHANNEL_KNOWLEDGE` and `SERIES_KNOWLEDGE`.

Searching the whole tree for readers turns up: the web UI listing `visual-bible.md` as a filename, and `packages/graphics` using an unrelated theme id that happens to be called `visual-bible-dark`. No stage, no prompt, no context assembly ever opens these files.

There is a structural reason it cannot be fixed by just reading them. A pipeline manifest's `inputs:` names artifact contracts produced by other stages (`contract: brief.md`). There is no slot for series- or channel-level knowledge. A stage cannot declare "I read the visual bible" even if someone wanted it to.

`studio/agent/src/context.ts` assembles a `ProductionContext` — pipeline, stages, budget, staleness, reviews. That is production *state*. None of it is creative *canon*.

## What to build

Add a `context:` block to the pipeline manifest naming channel and series knowledge a stage consumes, resolved through `layout.mjs` and frozen into `pipeline.snapshot.yaml` like every other binding. Canon then becomes what everything else already is: versioned, snapshot-frozen, reviewable production data — and a change to the bible invalidates the stages that read it, through the machinery that already exists.

## Why first

This is the cheapest high-value item in the epic and it gates two others. Interviewing the user at channel creation produces prose that nothing consumes until this exists, and consistent characters across episodes — the thing a series format is *for* — is not achievable without it.

title: Fill the compiler seat: something must compile the typed edit timeline
description:
Nothing compiles the typed edit timeline. This is the load-bearing gap: per-shot and per-frame creative control is not implementable until the timeline is the source of truth.

## What is actually there

`studio/contracts/schemas/v1alpha1/edit-timeline.schema.json` declares itself canonical. `packages/video-composer/src/validator.ts` validates it — 929 lines. Nothing consumes a `Timeline`. `packages/video-composer/src/composer.ts` is not exported from `src/index.ts` and takes a flat `SceneInput[]`.

What actually renders episodes is `composeEpisodeVideo()` in `studio/agent/src/capability-tools.ts`: `spawnSync` to ffmpeg, a glob over `assets/images`, narration WAVs concatenated, frame sizes normalised by hand. `pva_compose_video` calls it. So the arrangement ADR-0009 forbids is what ships.

Verified 2026-09-23: `SceneInput.transition` is declared at `composer.ts:24` and read nowhere else in the file; the filter graph is a plain `concat` with no `xfade`. Declared and ignored.

## Approach

`docs/notes/remotion-composer-design.md` (approved 2026-08-29, not implemented) argues for Remotion, on three grounds: motion and layout are cheap in React and painful as filter graphs; `packages/infographics` already renders on Remotion, so this removes a second engine rather than adding one; and the agent can author and preview React, which it cannot do with a filter graph.

Remotion Studio also gives live preview of a timeline essentially for free — which is what makes "discuss every frame" real rather than aspirational, and is the single biggest iteration-speed win available.

## Relationship to existing issues

This subsumes part of avg-z6c (recovered `packages/video-composer` work). Do not do these twice — decide per child whether it belongs to the ffmpeg composer or the new compiler:

- avg-z6c.4 transitions ignored, avg-z6c.6 segment captions, avg-z6c.7 narration/music/ducking/loudness: these are compiler features. If Remotion wins, they move here.
- avg-z6c.3 render report and delivery QA, avg-z6c.2 YouTube 1080p profile, avg-z6c.5 deterministic command preview: these outlive the engine choice.

avg-qr4.5 (shot and media-clip contracts) is the contract half of the same work and should be designed with this, not after it.

title: The workspace contract and the library disagree
description:
The workspace contract in `studio/contracts/src/layout.mjs` and the library on disk describe different trees. This is the root cause behind avg-t7i and avg-7he, and it will fail avg-fe2 for reasons already known.

## Measured across all 20 episodes on 2026-09-23

Episode manifest:

- 10 episodes have `episode.yaml` — what the contract names
- 11 have `episode.json` — which the contract does not mention
- 9 have neither

Directories, counted per episode:

| directory | episodes | in the contract |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts`, `assets` | 20 | yes |
| `reviews` | 18 | yes |
| `output` | 13 | yes |
| `production` | 12 | **no** |
| `journal` | 11 | yes |
| `source`, `prompts`, `attempts` | 10 | yes |
| `.snapshots`, `.revisions`, `private` | 1 each | **no** |

`production/` is in more episodes than `journal/` is. `giulio-cesare` keeps its animated scenes at `production/animated-scenes/s04.mp4`.

## Why this is the root cause, not a tidiness problem

`artifactExists` (avg-t7i) is not subtly wrong — it searches a set of paths that half the real work does not use. Fixing its three defects without reconciling the tree just moves the mismatch somewhere else. Same for avg-7he: an episode with no journal and an `episode.json` is not an anomaly, it is the majority case.

## What to decide

One way, not both:

1. The contract absorbs `production/` and `episode.json`, and `layout.mjs` grows accessors for them; or
2. A migration moves `production/` into `artifacts/` and converts `episode.json` to `episode.yaml`, the way `tools/migrate-library-layout.mjs` already moved the tree to layout 2 — idempotent, renames only, no media copied.

Option 2 is cleaner and there is precedent for it in the repo. Option 1 is cheaper and honest. Either is better than the current state, where the contract is aspirational and the code that trusts it reports finished stages as never-run.

Whichever is chosen, `studio/runtime/test/e2e/canonical-tree.test.ts` should pin the result against a real episode, not a synthesised one.

title: Creative control: the studio a person can direct
description:
The product direction from the 2026-09-22 report: make this a tool that produces high-quality video both on autopilot from a well-specified series, and under close human direction down to the individual shot.

The differentiators are real — open, local, filesystem-native, agentic, and formats (series) as a first-class concept. The thing that would quietly kill it is the agent becoming the monolith: `studio/agent/src/capability-tools.ts` already imports two providers directly and contains the ffmpeg composer that ADR-0009 was written to prevent. Every child here either pulls work out of that file or pushes more in. Prefer the ones that pull.

Ordering is deliberate and argued in `docs/notes/2026-09-22-stato-e-prospettive.md`. The two that unlock the rest are the timeline compiler and series canon reaching the prompt.

These are product goals, not defects. The stability work they sit on top of is tracked separately: avg-qr4.3 (approval), avg-t7i and avg-7he (artifact resolution), and the contract/library reconciliation.

title: artifactExists misses real artifacts in three ways, so finished stages report as never-run
description:
Found while reconstructing a journal for video-storici/roma-pills/giulio-cesare
(avg-7he). The runtime's artifactExists (studio/runtime/src/artifacts/discovery.ts:49)
reported 3 of that episode's 9 finished stages as having produced nothing. The
outputs are all on disk. Three independent causes:

1. NESTED OUTPUTS ARE UNREACHABLE. The candidate list is flat --
   artifacts/<label>, assets/<label>, output/<label> -- plus LEGACY_PATHS. The
   narration stage declares narration-manifest.json and narration-full.wav, which
   live at artifacts/narration/<label>. No candidate reaches one directory down.
   LEGACY_PATHS does map "narration.mp3", but no manifest in the repo declares
   that label, so the entry is dead and the live labels are unresolvable.

2. A LEGACY MAPPING POINTS AT A DIRECTORY NOTHING WRITES. "illustrations/" maps
   to artifacts/frames, which does not exist on this episode; the images are at
   assets/images/s1.png ... CAPABILITY_PATHS has no "illustrations/" entry.

3. THE CURRENT-RENDER POINTER IS READ RELATIVE TO THE WRONG DIRECTORY.
   currentRenderExists (discovery.ts:34) does path.join(episodeDir, "output",
   pointer.path). Real pointers write path relative to the EPISODE:
   output/current.json on this episode holds "path": "output/final.mp4", so the
   check looks for <episode>/output/output/final.mp4 and misses a render that is
   present. Either the writer or this reader is wrong about the base; they must
   agree. Affects every label routed through output/current.json -- output.mp4
   and final-video.mp4.

Impact is bounded but real: avg-grf's final review confirmed artifactExists is on
NO execution path, so this cannot cause a stage to re-run. It is a REPORTING
defect -- discovery, doctor and workspace read it, so the studio's view of an
episode can claim nothing was produced while the files sit there. It also makes
any artifact-based reasoning about existing episodes (including a journal
backfill for avg-7he) wrong by default.

Verified by reconstruction: with the three locations added, giulio-cesare
resolves 9 of 10 stages, and the only genuinely absent output is tapes/ for
terminal-recordings -- an episode about Julius Caesar has no terminal to record.

title: Existing episodes have no journal, so /execute restarts them from the first stage
description:
avg-2n7 moved the gateway's /execute onto the execution service, which derives state by replaying the episode journal. The route it replaced asked the runtime CLI, which picks the first stage whose declared outputs are absent on disk.

All 20 episodes under library/ have real artifacts and ZERO journal events — verified by counting. So after avg-2n7 merges, /execute on any of them re-selects the first stage, finds no handler, and returns '0 completed, 1 blocked' no matter how finished the episode actually is. Not destructive, but the route does nothing useful on any existing episode.

Deliberately NOT fixed in avg-2n7: a backfill that synthesises stage-completed events from which output files exist would reintroduce file-existence inference into the exact system built to remove it, and inventing history is worse than having none.

Options worth weighing: a one-time, explicitly human-invoked migration command that is honest about what it is inferring; accepting that existing episodes restart; or treating the library's contents as disposable fixtures. The right answer depends on whether those 20 episodes are real work or test data, which the issue's owner knows and this analysis does not.

The test suite cannot see this — every route test hand-seeds a journal.
notes:
Reconstruction done for ONE episode as a sample: video-storici/roma-pills/giulio-cesare.
27 events, 9 of 10 stages completed, terminal-recordings genuinely never ran (no tapes).
`vpr status` now replays it correctly: 9 completed, 1 pending, and four stages sitting at
awaiting_review because they declare review: human and no approval record exists (avg-qr4.3).

Corrections to this issue's premise, both verified:
- The journals are not all absent. TEN episodes have a zero-byte journal/events.jsonl and ten
  have no journal directory at all. "Zero events" is right; "no journal" is not.
- Pipelines resolve at the SERIES level, not the episode. Only 3 episodes name a pipeline
  themselves; 16 of 20 inherit one from their series' pipeline.yaml. The 4 under quiet-cosmos
  and studio-tests resolve nothing, so no journal can be reconstructed for them -- replay needs
  the declared stage ids.

How the reconstruction stays honest, since this IS the file-existence inference qr4.2 removed:
every event carries reconstructed: true, reconstructedFrom: "artifact-mtime", and the
observedMtime it was derived from; actor is `system` and holder is "system/journal-backfill",
never `runtime`. Artifact mtimes set the CLOCK but never the ORDER -- events are emitted in
topological order with each timestamp clamped after its predecessor, because mtimes contradict
dependency order after re-runs (on this episode qa's mtime precedes captions' by 28 minutes).

Blocked on avg-t7i for the rest: artifactExists misses nested outputs, maps illustrations/ to a
directory nothing writes, and reads the current-render pointer relative to the wrong base. The
backfill had to add those three locations itself to see 9 stages instead of 6.

Script (not committed, library/ is gitignored):
.../scratchpad/backfill-journal.mjs -- dry-runs by default, --write to append.

title: appendJournalEvent silently drops a malformed execution event
description:
studio/contracts/src/journal.mjs appendJournalEvent catches build errors and returns null rather than throwing. That contract is deliberate and documented — a stage that ran must not be reported failed because its bookkeeping could not be written — and it was right while the journal was a narrative.

It is no longer sufficient. avg-pm8 made execution state a replay of this journal, so a dropped stage-leased or stage-completed is lost EXECUTION STATE, not a lost note. Every gateway call site ignores the return value; only studio/runtime/src/cli.ts:434 checks it.

Deliberately not changed in avg-pm8: the never-throw contract is relied on by today's callers, and avg-tt7 (the execution service) is the first caller for which a silent null is a correctness bug. Settle the policy there, with its consumers in view, rather than changing it underneath the current ones. Options: a throwing variant for execution events, or making the service check the return.

Raised by the final whole-branch review of avg-pm8 and sharpened by its fix wave.

title: CLI and agent speak the execution service, not their own dialects
description:

vpr run is advisory: it prints 'Ready to execute: <stage>' with an instruction for the Pi agent and persists nothing. cmdStatus infers completion from output-file existence and emits a zero-consumption budget. cmdRerun returns an empty plan. studio/agent/src/pipeline-tools.ts describes its tools as executing and waiting, which the runtime does not do.

title: Vertical slice: one real episode end-to-end through the real architecture
description:
One real episode produced end to end through the real architecture, with zero fabricated artifacts. This is the acceptance test for the whole system, and it is still not met.

## Why it is still open, with evidence from 2026-09-23

The library holds 20 episodes and several have rendered MP4s, so it is easy to believe this is done. It is not: the renders came from the older ad-hoc path, not the architecture.

Taking `library/childrens/series/fairy-tales/episodes/sleeping-beauty` as the example — it has a finished `output/dawn-garden-1786816607243-302a1cb5.mp4` and an `output/current.json` pointing at it:

- it carries `episode.json`, where the contract names `episode.yaml`
- it has **no journal at all**, so nothing about how it was made is derivable
- its render report holds `version, renderId, sourceVideo, cueSheet, output, createdAt` — no QA verdict, so `current.json` does not point at a QA-passed render, it points at the last render
- it keeps work in `production/`, a directory the workspace contract does not name

Across the whole library: 10 episodes have `episode.yaml`, 11 have `episode.json`, 9 have neither, and only 10 have `journal/events.jsonl`.

## What the slice must show

Init channel, series and episode through the runtime; snapshot the pipeline; run the stages through the one execution service that avg-2n7 and avg-grf built, so every stage leaves journal events; illustrations through `packages/fal-media` with provider-job records; narration through `packages/voice`; captions; an edit timeline; composition through the composer rather than the agent's private `composeEpisodeVideo`; QA gates that can actually fail. `output/current.json` points at a render that passed QA. The episode is browsable in `studio/web` with real token auth.

Replaying that episode's journal must reconstruct its full state, and `vpr status` must agree with what is on disk.

## Ordering

This is the acceptance test, not the first task. It should be attempted after the workspace contract and the library agree (`episode.yaml` vs `episode.json`, `production/`) and after the composer seat is filled — otherwise it fails for reasons that are already known and already filed.

title: Uniform generative provenance: seed, model, prompt, per artifact
description:
`pipeline.snapshot.yaml` freezes contract versions, provider bindings and skill identities. That is enough to reproduce an *editorial* decision and not enough to reproduce a *generated* one.

Reproducibility with generative providers needs, recorded per artifact and uniformly across every provider: the model identity and version, the seed, the full prompt as sent, and the provider's own job id. `packages/fal-media` records provenance and cost; `packages/codex-image` and the Blender and graphics paths do not do it the same way, so there is no single place to read the answer.

## Make it a conformance requirement

avg-qr4.4 (declarative adapter registry) and avg-50j (adapter conformance kit) are where this belongs: "add a provider" should mean "pass the suite", and the suite should refuse a provider that cannot say how to reproduce its own output.

## Acceptance

"Regenerate shot 4 exactly as it was" is answerable from the artifact alone, for every capability that generates media, without knowing which provider produced it.

title: Budget must be released, reconciled, and visible per series
description:
`BudgetGuard` exists, its reservations leak (avg-91o), and no surface shows a number. Autopilot without a visible ceiling is the failure mode that costs real money before anyone notices.

## Three parts

1. **Fix the leak.** avg-91o: reservations are taken by `maySpend` and nothing releases them. Note the constraint already recorded in `studio/runtime/src/execution/types.ts`: `status()` deliberately does not ask the guard for a verdict, because minting a reservation on every polled read would be worse than the disagreement it removes. A release path is the precondition for ever relaxing that.

2. **Record actual spend, not just estimates.** avg-a83.2 (recovered `fma-9km.7`, "estimate, reserve, and reconcile fal spend") is the provider half and is unimplemented — nothing in `packages/fal-media/src` mentions reserve or reconcile. Verified 2026-09-23.

3. **Show it per series and per episode.** A limit, what it has consumed, what a pending run would add. In the CLI status output and in `studio/web`.

## Why per series

Because the series is where autopilot instructions live, so it is where a ceiling means something. A per-episode cap does not stop a run of ten.

title: Autopilot intake: series source handlers and a queue
description:
"Generate ten videos from these ten links, you know how to handle them because the series says so" needs two things that do not exist: a series-level source handler and a queue.

Today you would create ten episodes by hand. The series layout already has a `sources/` directory — empty, read by nothing, the same story as the visual bible.

## What is missing

A source handler declared at series level that says what an input *is* and how it becomes an episode: a URL to fetch and summarise, a document, a repository, a list. Given ten inputs it produces ten episodes with their briefs seeded, and enqueues them.

A queue with a concurrency limit, because ten episodes running at once against a rate-limited provider is not ten times faster. `avg-qr4.7` (durable bounded workers) is the execution half and should be built with this, not separately.

A visible ceiling, because this is the mode that spends money unattended. See the budget issue.

## Acceptance

One command, ten links, ten episodes that each stop at their first review gate — and a single place showing what each one cost and where it stopped.

title: Scratch workspaces: immediate work without ceremony, on the same spine
description:
Let a user work on a scene or a shot immediately, with whatever tool they like, without creating a channel and a series and a pipeline first — and without forking the system into two execution models.

## The redirect

The request was "without following a pipeline, without staying in a series". That is the right user experience and the wrong implementation. A genuinely pipeline-free mode has no journal, no provenance, no leases and no review — which discards exactly what avg-2n7, avg-grf and avg-0v5 were built to provide, and creates a second execution path that will drift from the first.

## Instead

A scratch workspace is a real episode whose pipeline is trivial: `library/_scratch/<name>/`, running a `freeform` manifest with one editorial stage, `autopilot: false`, and arbitrary capability calls permitted. Everything is journaled. Nothing about the spine changes.

`_` is already reserved for holding areas at every level of the layout (`_media`, `_exports`), so the root needs no new convention.

Promotion matters as much as creation: a scratch workspace that turns into something should be movable into a real series without losing its journal.

title: Interview the user at channel and series creation, and author the pipeline
description:
When a user creates a channel or a series, interview them properly, and produce two things: populated canon, and a pipeline designed for that format.

Today `pva_create_channel` and `pva_create_series` scaffold empty directories and a one-line `visual-bible.md`. Nobody is asked anything.

## The interview

Audience, tone, language, length target, cadence, visual identity, voice, recurring characters, what the format never does. The answers are written into the knowledge files the series already has slots for — which is why this depends on canon actually being read by stages.

## The second half, which is the larger one

"Design a precise pipeline that follows conventions" means pipeline authoring becomes an agent capability. Today there are four hand-written YAML manifests in `studio/pipelines/pipelines/`. The guardrails to generate against already exist: the schema, the linter, and the valid/invalid fixture pairs in `studio/pipelines/fixtures/` (`pipeline-empty-stages`, `unknown-capability`, `pipeline-leaked-orchestration`, `stage-missing-type`).

A generated pipeline must validate against the same rules a hand-written one does, and must be written to the series' own `pipelines/` directory, where series-local overrides already resolve.

## Depends on

Series canon reaching the prompt. Without it the interview writes files nothing opens, which is the current state with extra steps.

title: A developer side-agent for this repository
description:
A side agent that knows this repository as a developer of it, so work on the studio itself can continue alongside work in it.

Everything it needs already exists and is unusually well suited to this: the beads tracker, 33 ADRs recording decisions and their reasons, `docs/superpowers/specs/` and `docs/superpowers/plans/` holding the design history, and the brainstorm to spec to plan to subagent-execution workflow this project actually uses.

## Shape

A Pi extension plus a skill carrying the repository's conventions: the ADR trail, the package boundaries enforced by `tools/check-boundaries.mjs`, the per-package test commands and their traps (`studio/runtime` has a `pretest` build and its integration tests spawn `dist/`, so a bare vitest run passes against stale output; `studio/web` uses bun; `studio/contracts` has no build step), and the documentation rule that VitePress compiles every `docs/` markdown as a Vue component, so a bare angle-bracket word in prose breaks the site.

## Why early

title: BudgetGuard reservations are taken and never released
description:
studio/runtime/src/execution/service.ts calls BudgetGuard.maySpend and discards the returned Reservation. Reservation carries a reserveId, so any real guard that actually reserves will leak one on every blocked and failed call — and on every dry run, which avg-tt7's spec promises makes no paid calls.

No BudgetGuard implementation exists yet, so avg-tt7 deliberately did not invent a release API: whoever writes the first guard is better placed to decide whether the service should call release on a non-completion, consume on a completion, or whether the guard should own its own lifecycle. studio/runtime/src/policy/ledger.ts already has reserveBudget/consumeReserve/releaseReserve as unwired functions and is the obvious starting point.

Raised by the final whole-branch review of avg-tt7 and parked there.
notes:
avg-grf confirmed the leak's shape and deliberately did not widen it.

BudgetGuard has exactly one method, maySpend -- no release, no settle. So a reservation a
claim() mints cannot be settled through the port at all; complete() has no way to return it.
(I ruled the opposite mid-branch and retracted it the same day after checking the interface:
reserveBudget/consumeReserve/releaseReserve exist as real functions with no store and no
callers.)

One consequence worth keeping: the precheck in claimInternal sits ABOVE the budget checks, not
below. Below would have minted a reservation and then refused on a condition knowable first --
widening this leak and changing refusal precedence. Anything that reorders those gates has to
account for that.

title: Root npm test flakes under concurrency; per-package suites are green
description:
Running npm test at the repo root runs the package suites concurrently, and timeout-bound tests fail under that load. Observed across several runs on the same commit: 13 passed/0 failed, then 12/1 (studio/agent), then 11/2 (studio/agent + studio/gateway).

Run serially, every package passes: contracts 116/116, runtime 360/360, gateway 278/278, agent 184/184.

The tests that flake are the ones with short fixed timeouts:
- studio/agent tests/production.test.ts and tests/e2e-scenarios.test.ts — 'extension module can be imported' and 'extension exports a default factory', 5000ms, both timing out on a module import
- studio/agent tests/capability-layout.test.ts — 'writes the narration manifest inside the episode'
- studio/gateway test/integration.test.ts — afterAll hook, 30000ms

Not caused by avg-pm8: reproduced on the merge base ed62910 with the same command and the same node_modules (1 failure there, 0 on the branch, on back-to-back runs).

Worth fixing because it makes the aggregate suite untrustworthy as a merge gate — the signal a reviewer most wants is the one that flakes. Options: raise the timeouts on import-bound tests, mark them serial, or limit root-level concurrency.
notes:
Quantified 2026-09-21: studio/gateway test/integration.test.ts's boot hook times out with ZERO
failing assertions in roughly 1 run of 6. Reproduced 2 times in 8 runs on commit 504b0c1 with an
in-flight branch's files removed, so it is neither the root runner nor any current work — it is
that file's own boot/teardown being load-sensitive.

Practical effect: a green per-package gateway run is not reliably reproducible, and a red one is
not evidence of a regression. Anyone bisecting or gating on this suite should re-run before
believing a failure whose output shows no failed assertion.
Third sighting on the avg-grf branch, and the shape is consistent: test/integration.test.ts
reports a FILE-level failure -- "Hook timed out in 30000ms" -- while all 324 tests pass. Not a
test assertion failing; a hook. Duration on the failing run was 108s vs ~17-33s when green.

Frequency held at roughly 1 in 3 to 1 in 6 across this branch's runs. Never reproducible on
retry: two further full suites and three repeats of the file were clean each time.

The 30s hookTimeout and whatever the beforeAll/afterAll actually waits on are the place to look.

title: POST /execute returns ok:true when no stage could be run
description:
studio/gateway/src/routes/production.ts derives ok from the count of failed stages. A run that reached no stage at all — vpr unreachable, or a runtime response the executor cannot parse — produces an empty stage list, so ok is true.

report.summary is now honest about this (avg-qr4.1 commit 697a97e stopped it claiming 'All stages already complete'), but the HTTP field a caller is most likely to branch on still says success.

Deliberate and correct for blocked/awaiting_approval — a halt at a review gate is not a failure. The gap is specifically the reached-nothing case.

Found during avg-qr4.1's final review; parked there because the workflow allows a single fix wave.

title: Journal read failure fails open in the gateway's dependency gate
description:
studio/gateway/src/runtime/executor.ts readJournal() catches any read or parse failure and returns no events, so blockingDependency() returns null and the stage runs. Every other unknown in this dispatcher fails closed.

Narrow in practice: an absent journal is the normal first-run case and must not block, and parseJournal already skips individually corrupt lines, so this only bites when the file is wholly unreadable (permissions, truncation mid-write). description:
The extensibility gap named in the 2026-08-14 review. The stated goal is many more pipeline steps and providers, but every adapter is bespoke and nothing proves a new one behaves. ADR-0015 says stages request capabilities not providers — today that contract is enforced by nobody.

The raw material already exists: video-workspace-contracts/fixtures/ has valid/invalid pairs across 13 schema families, plus 14 check-*.mjs scripts that only run inside the contracts module.

Steps:

2. Export assertCapabilityConformance(capability, adapter) covering: provider-job record shape, provenance and cost fields, idempotency, cancellation, and the no-silent-fallback rule from ARCHITECTURE.md.
3. Have fal-media-adapter, ffmpeg-video-composer, studio-graphics-renderer, and the qwen-tts HTTP client each call it in their own test suite.

title: A git repository per channel, editorial layer only
description:
A git repository per channel, committing the channel's changes — with a hard rule about what is committed.

## The constraint that makes or breaks it

ADR-0021: generated media is immutable and not auto-committed. `giulio-cesare` alone holds a dozen MP4s. A repository that commits "changes" becomes unusable within a few episodes.

**Commit the editorial and declarative layer only:** `episode.yaml`, `pipeline.snapshot.yaml`, briefs, scripts, art direction, the edit timeline, `journal/events.jsonl`, reviews, and the channel and series knowledge files. Never media — that stays content-addressed on disk and referenced by hash.

## What it buys

Diffable creative history. Branch an episode to try a different cut. Revert a script without touching the renders it produced. A channel becomes portable and shareable without shipping gigabytes, which suits an open local tool better than a database would.

## Ordering

After the timeline compiler, because the timeline is the artifact most worth versioning and its absence is what makes the current tree hard to diff meaningfully.

Note the interaction with the root repository: `library/` is gitignored here, so a per-channel repository nests inside an ignored directory. That is workable but must be deliberate — decide whether these are independent repositories or submodules before writing code.

title: narrated-illustrated-video minDuration 180s conflicts with actual TTS pacing

## Fix
Either: (a) calibrate script word budget against actual TTS wpm (measured ~175 wpm for Qwen3 default voice), or (b) lower minDuration to 150s for quick overviews, or (c) add speed: option to pipeline narration config (e.g., 0.92 gives ~170s).

title: StageExecutor is now dead code and invites recreating the split
description:
studio/runtime/src/engine/executor.ts (StageExecutor) has no production callers and, after avg-tt7, is unlikely ever to gain one: the execution service does its job using StageStateMachine and FileLock directly, writing through @studio/contracts' journal.

StageExecutor's only distinct contributions are a dependency on studio/runtime/src/journal/ — the second, parallel journal with a dotted vocabulary that deriveExecutionState does not read — and an initStages that duplicates what replay already does. Wiring it up would send execution writes to a log nothing can recover state from, which is exactly the split avg-qr4.2 exists to close.

Leaving a second executor in the tree invites someone to wire it up later. Consider deleting StageExecutor and, with it, the parallel journal module — or, if its sequence numbers and SHA-256 hash chain are worth keeping, port those onto the contracts journal instead (slice A's spec flagged that a load-bearing log deserves better than a plain append) and delete the rest.

Raised in avg-tt7's spec as an explicit out-of-scope risk.
notes:
New fact from avg-grf, and it raises the stakes: the three dead parallel implementations are
EXPORTED FROM @studio/runtime's PUBLIC BARREL. An external consumer can reach a second journal
(studio/runtime/src/journal/, dotted vocabulary, own writer/reader/projections), a second
stage-run loop (StageExecutor), and a second gate evaluator (checkGate/checkGates).

None is on any execution path -- avg-grf's final review confirmed one FileLock, one
deriveExecutionState, one service factory per process, and four journal appends all inside
claim/complete/recordFailure. They are husks, but reachable husks with their own green test
suites, which is exactly what invites someone to wire one up and recreate the three-way split
avg-qr4.2 exists to close.

Deliberately NOT deleted in avg-grf (Ruling 26): three tested modules removed in the last hour
of a 34-commit branch, seen by one review pass, is how something breaks quietly. This issue is
where they go.

title: Lease-takeover tests are wall-clock timed and may flake on loaded CI
description:
studio/runtime/test/unit/execution/concurrency.test.ts and fail-closed.test.ts pin lease-takeover and lease-expiry behaviour using real timers: a 25ms TTL against a 60ms gap and a 250ms dispatch. The margins are 2.4x and 10x, and five local repeats showed no flakes — but sub-50ms wall-clock TTLs are a known flake vector on throttled or contended CI runners.

If these ever flake, do not widen the margins reflexively; the service takes an injectable clock (ExecutionServiceOptions.now), so the honest fix is to drive these tests from a fake clock rather than from wall time. That was not done during avg-tt7 because the lock's own expiry is filesystem-mtime based and does not read that clock, so it would have required changing FileLock too.

Raised by the final fix-wave re-review of avg-tt7.

title: Only two of five execution-event payloads have positive fixtures

title: parseJournal strict mode validates syntax, not event shape
description:
studio/contracts/src/journal.mjs parseJournal({ strict: true }) throws on a line that is not valid JSON, but any valid-JSON line passes through: parseJournal('123\n', { strict: true }) returns [123], typed JournalEvent[].

Harmless today — deriveExecutionState ignores anything that is not a known execution event type — but the return type claims more than it delivers, and strict mode exists precisely for callers deriving state from the log.
